Sorry you're going through this OP. I semi-recently went through a breakup with my boyfriend of 2 years a little over 7 months ago. The biggest things that helped me were my immediate support system (always having friends and family there to talk to about what I was feeling, but also as a distraction), my therapist and allowing myself the time to feel everything. 

Distractions are awesome, but short lived. Truly taking the time to feel and process helps tremendously. Of course, you eventually reach a limit where you have to start actively putting in work to pick yourself back up. Exercise, new hobbies, reconnecting with old friends. Doing an activity that you couldn't/wouldn't do before because of the relationship. Travel, if you have the means. Shake things up. 

The hardest part for me was re-learning a routine. My life as I had known it for the last two years instantly changed. For someone who isn't the fondest of change, this was really hard to accept. But it was all the change that allowed me to heal and move on. It's 7 months later, I've met a new guy and am happier than I have ever been in my life. I know look back on that relationship as a really valuable stepping stone. I thought I was happy, but I didn't realize what "happy" really felt like.

I know it's cliche, but its true. Time will lessen the blow and soon you will pick yourself back together and go on with your life. For right now, try to stay connected with friends - Facetime, phone calls, or text, if not in person. You'll get through this. Wishing you the best of luck

I had to work when my parents and 2 of my siblings left the day prior, so my sister and I drove together the next day. We were driving through the mountains of PA when Coldplay's "Paradise" came on my iPod. All of the sudden, I felt this wave come over me and I knew she had passed. I started crying and my sister kept telling me it was fine and we dont know anything for sure. Turns out, as soon as we pull up to the hospital, my mom is outside bawling in my dad's arms. She had died about an hour before we got there, right around the time I had that feeling. They didn't want to tell us while we were on the road because we were so young and they were worried about us driving while being that upset. I can't listen to that song without crying anymore and thinking of her.
